title: Thinner Corneas Appear to Have More Striking Effects of Corneal Collagen Crosslinking in Patients with Progressive Keratoconus

groups.description: Group 1: preoperative thinnest corneal thickness <= 400 um (Methods: less than 400 um); 31 eyes (Table 2 header); Epithelium-off Dresden CXL (epithelium removed over 9 mm, 0.1% riboflavin every 3 min for 30 min, UVA 370 nm 3.0 mW/cm2 for 30 min; hypo-osmolar 0.1% riboflavin until 400 um when the denuded cornea was thinner than 400 um) for progressive keratoconus; no cataract or other surgery in the described session

Group 2: preoperative thinnest corneal thickness > 400 um and <= 450 um (Methods: between 400 and 450 um); 41 eyes (Table 2 header); Epithelium-off Dresden CXL (epithelium removed over 9 mm, 0.1% riboflavin every 3 min for 30 min, UVA 370 nm 3.0 mW/cm2 for 30 min; hypo-osmolar 0.1% riboflavin until 400 um when the denuded cornea was thinner than 400 um) for progressive keratoconus; no cataract or other surgery in the described session

Group 3: preoperative thinnest corneal thickness > 450 um and <= 500 um (Methods: between 450 and 500 um); 36 eyes (Table 2 header); Epithelium-off Dresden CXL (epithelium removed over 9 mm, 0.1% riboflavin every 3 min for 30 min, UVA 370 nm 3.0 mW/cm2 for 30 min; hypo-osmolar 0.1% riboflavin until 400 um when the denuded cornea was thinner than 400 um) for progressive keratoconus; no cataract or other surgery in the described session

Group 4: preoperative thinnest corneal thickness >= 500 um (Methods: 500 um or more); 15 eyes (Table 2 header); Epithelium-off Dresden CXL (epithelium removed over 9 mm, 0.1% riboflavin every 3 min for 30 min, UVA 370 nm 3.0 mW/cm2 for 30 min; hypo-osmolar 0.1% riboflavin until 400 um when the denuded cornea was thinner than 400 um) for progressive keratoconus; no cataract or other surgery in the described session

exclusions.what: Whole-cohort BCVA of all 123 eyes (Table 1 row 7: preop, 6 and 12 months)
exclusions.reason: the same eyes are tabulated by preoperative thinnest-corneal-thickness subgroup in Table 2; the subgroups are extracted and the whole-cohort series is not (brief: no whole-cohort series alongside its preoperative-condition subgroups); the 6-month visit exists only for the whole cohort

notes: 123 eyes of 101 patients; the Results give the group sizes 31/41/36/15 as 'patients', but they sum to 123 and match the Table 2 header n, so they are eyes.
The abstract and the Methods word the thickness boundaries slightly differently (abstract: <=400, 400-450, 450-500, >=500 um).
Contact lens wear was discontinued before each evaluation (Methods).
Tables 1-2 also tabulate thinnest corneal thickness, K1, K2, Kmax, uncorrected acuity (logMAR), IOP and endothelial cell density; Tables 3-4 tabulate the change in Kmax; none of these is used.
